FISHING LICENCE · UNITED STATES

Pennsylvania fishing licence

Anglers aged 16 or older need a fishing licence. The one-day tourist licence includes trout and Lake Erie permits but is invalid March 15–April 30.

Official rules ↗

Updated 2026-11-11

Who needs one

  • Residents and visitors aged 16 or older, unless exempt.

Who doesn’t

  • Children under 16; special mentored youth events can require a youth permit.

Licence options and prices

LicenceForLengthPrice
Non-resident 1-day touristnon resident1 day; unavailable March 15–April 30$31.97 USD
Non-resident 3-day touristnon resident3 days$31.97 USD
Non-resident 7-day touristnon resident7 days$39.47 USD
Non-resident annualnon resident2026 licence year$60.97 USD

Extra stamps and permits

  • Trout Permit · $14.97 USD
    Required for trout fishing unless exempt or included in the selected licence.
  • Lake Erie Permit · $9.97 USD
    Required for Lake Erie, Presque Isle Bay, and their tributaries, unless exempt or included.
  • Combination Trout/Lake Erie Permit · $20.97 USD
    Combined coverage when both permits are needed.

Rules visitors should know

  • The one-day tourist licence includes both named permits.
  • Listed prices include the issuing-agent and transaction fees.

How to buy

Use the PFBC online purchase link or a fishing licence issuing agent.

Common license questions

Do I need a fishing licence in Pennsylvania?

Anglers aged 16 or older need a fishing licence. The one-day tourist licence includes trout and Lake Erie permits but is invalid March 15–April 30.

How much is a visitor fishing licence in Pennsylvania?

Non-resident 1-day tourist: $31.97 USD; Non-resident 3-day tourist: $31.97 USD; Non-resident 7-day tourist: $39.47 USD; Non-resident annual: $60.97 USD (checked November 2026).

Where do I buy a fishing licence in Pennsylvania?

Use the PFBC online purchase link or a fishing licence issuing agent.
